classification.difficultyReason: Model two tariffs, find their equal-cost point and distinguish equality from becoming more expensive.

content.prompt: Andrew and a group of his friends have decided they want to race go-karts on the weekend, and Andrew wants to work out which of the two local go-kart places will be cheaper. Kart-Kingdom charges $\$15$ per person to do safety training, and then 50 cents per lap that you do. Go-Mobile charges 80 cents per lap, and the safety training is free. After how many laps does Go-Mobile become more expensive than Kart-Kingdom?

answer.short:
More than 50 laps; the first whole-lap total is 51 laps.

The costs are equal at 50 laps, and Go-Mobile costs more for each additional lap.
answer.worked:
Let $x$ be the number of laps per person. In dollars, Kart-Kingdom costs $15+0.50x$ and Go-Mobile costs $0.80x$.

Find when the costs are equal:

$$\begin{align*}15+0.50x&=0.80x\\15&=0.30x\\x&=\frac{15}{0.30}\\x&=50\end{align*}$$

At 50 laps, each costs $\$40$. Go-Mobile charges 30 cents more for each additional lap, so it becomes more expensive after 50 laps. At 51 laps, Go-Mobile costs $\$40.80$ and Kart-Kingdom costs $\$40.50$.
